floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 24 confirmed (75 vs 77 insns); residual isolated to 4 families; named-intermediate lever reaches 77/77 insn parity (score 33) and biv-elimination confirmed as the cause of the folded stor
Floor 24 -> 20: D1 and D3 both closed and target's exact register assignment reached at build_insns 77 == target_insns 77; residual is the $v0/$v1 mirror in the if-arms plus preheader order.

Floor held at 20 (77/77 insns); eleven structural variants measured and killed, and D2's mechanism corrected from a local-alloc combine_regs tie to a global.c allocno_compare contest between exactly t

Floor 20 -> 18: a permuter-found, hand-minimised per-loop carrier re-home (the 0x20-bits_left shift amount computed into the other bit loop's dead walking pointer, plus a second holder for 'needed') c

frontier.hypothesis: D2 (14 of the remaining 18 points) closes only if 'hi' gains enough references to cross a floor_log2 bucket and outrank 'val' in global.c allocno_compare; every route that removes or re-homes val's references is now measured dead.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare priority = floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs/livelen; val = nrefs 19 / livelen 15 / pri 50666 takes $v1, hi = nrefs 8 / livelen 18 / pri 13333 takes $v0, and target needs the reverse. vL (session 3) proved removing val's refs kills D1; session 4 proved a read-back re-home changes nothing.
frontier.next_probe: (a) The one unexecuted F1(a) probe: spell the store as 'hi = (hi << needed) | (cur >> bits_left); *(s16 *)(dst + 0xA) = (s16)hi;' so hi gains two refs per arm (8 -> ~16, crossing into floor_log2 4) with val untouched; (b) shorten hi's livelen of 18 by moving the 'cur = *arg1;' refill out of hi's span; (c) read the ALLOCDBG pri column (tmp/grind/func_8001979C/s3/qty.sh) for every variant - it is a far finer gradient than the sandbox score.

frontier.hypothesis: D4's remaining 4 points are purely the walking-pointer init's POSITION (ours before the sw/lw preamble, target's last in the preheader), and it can only move if the counter/walker priority window is widened from the counter's side.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c move_movables / scan_loop choose the preheader insertion point, and global.c allocno_compare fixes what may move: counter nrefs 21 / livelen 60 / pri 14000, each walker nrefs 13; moving an init late costs livelen and flips the walker above the counter (session 2's P6, score 31). The 'li' order half of D4 closed this session as a side effect of the allocation change.
frontier.next_probe: (a) Find a change that lengthens the counter's live range without dropping it a floor_log2 bucket, then re-test the late walker init; (b) read tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c move_movables / scan_loop to find where the preheader insertion point is chosen relative to the loop's first insn, and whether the walker init is a movable at all in this form.

frontier.hypothesis: The closing form's policy status is the binding gate on any candidate-ready, and it now covers TWO constructs, not one.
frontier.mechanism: The duplicated 'dst += 2' is byte-neutral (proven) and its measurable effect is loop.c biv_count; the session-4 carrier reuse writes a later-live walking pointer with an unrelated value purely for allocation pressure. Both are claims on the frozen 'variable reuse for codegen control' / 'duplicated-statement-into-arms' families, and a claim is not a finding.
frontier.next_probe: Read .claude/rules/duplicated-statement-into-arms.md and the frozen list in .claude/rules/no-new-park-categories.md; quote each scope sentence VERBATIM into memory/grind/func_8001979C/self_vet.md paired with a file:line or commit-hash precedent. If either scope does not cleanly cover its construct - in particular the carrier reuse, which has no precedent in this ledger - emit ruling-request rather than a submission.
